newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end mixed, focus on power sector.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end mixed, focus on power sector.

text.p: Ignoring Wall Street's surge, Chilean shares closed narrowly mixed with all eyes focussed on electricity shares on talk that Spanish state power utility Endesa is buying shares in the sector, said traders.
Stocks are seen staging a mild rally at the opening buoyed by speculation over electrcity stocks, they said.
"It could rise a little. The Endesa talk means there could be more international interest in Chile," said one dealer.
The selective IPSA index closed down 0.07 percent at 97.65 points. The general IGPA index rose 0.05 percent at 5,347.16 points.
Turnover dropped to seven billion pesos from 14.4 billion pesos Friday.
Traders said Endesa was buying shares in the Chispa group of investment companies -- controllers of power utility Enersis -- and may issue a formal offer for more stock.
If Endesa buys up 50 percent of the group's stock, including Chispa One, Chispa Two, Almendros and Luz, it would give the Spanish utility control of about 10 percent of Enersis, said traders.
Endesa is planning to invest $600 million in Chile, they said.
The Chispa group said in a statement to the stock exchange last week that it did know why its stock rallied when talk of a deal with Endesa emerged.
Chispa One closed up 0.7 percent at 181 pesos, while Enersis was unchanged at 252 pesos.
Other risers included Telex, up 1.69 percent at 1,200 pesos, and bottler Andina, which gained 0.65 percent to 2,340 pesos.
Losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 1.95 percent at 201 pesos, steelmaker Cap, down 0.79 percent at 1,260 pesos, and glass company Cristales, which shed 0.7 percent at 2,830 pesos.
